purpose: Record only residual novelty candidates after subtracting established prior art. These are candidates for later K1-K9 falsification, not final novelty conclusions.

candidates.contribution: Systematic model-form error and validity-domain map for baseline M1 across layer count N, vacuum pressure p_vac, and bending severity/curvature kappa, against an interface-resolved reference R.

known_overlap.overlap: Continuum/global-local model versus discrete-contact reference with quantitative error boundary over layer count/rotation; no vacuum-pressure sweep and no physical boundary-crossing experiment.
Continuum layer-jamming homogenization; no structural validity-domain map or physical validation.
Baseline continuum layer-jamming beam model M1; does not provide systematic breakdown map.

threats: K9 conceptual equivalence under different terminology
kill_conditions: Prior art performs a substantially equivalent validity-domain map for a vacuum layer-jamming continuum beam across the relevant operating domain.
Existing evidence shows the proposed error-map act is only a routine replication of ca46dc062d with no mechanics-specific new question.

candidates.contribution: Experimental tests deliberately sampling both sides of a predicted M1 validity/breakdown boundary under vacuum layer-jamming, with model parameters and acceptance criteria frozen before evaluation.

known_overlap.overlap: Physical layer-jamming bending experiments and model comparison, but not a predicted continuum-model breakdown boundary.
Experimental validation of slip/hysteresis, but not boundary-crossing validity testing of M1.
Quantitative numerical boundary mapping, but no physical experiments and no vacuum-jamming pressure sweep.

threats: K5 physical sampling on both sides of boundary
kill_conditions: Prior art already performs boundary-crossing physical experiments for the same or conceptually equivalent vacuum layer-jamming continuum model.
The proposed experiment does not test a pre-specified boundary and reduces to ordinary model validation.

candidates.contribution: Mechanistic attribution of M1 breakdown to interface-resolved slip/contact/normal-pressure redistribution, rather than reporting error alone.

known_overlap.overlap: Mechanistically links layer-jamming stiffness/hysteresis to interlayer slip.
Links multilayer continuum error to interface slip in non-vacuum structures.
Full-layer contact model captures frictional hysteresis in unbonded flexible pipes.

threats: K6 mechanism attribution already established for same scientific act
kill_conditions: A prior study already explains failure of a comparable vacuum layer-jamming continuum beam model using interface-resolved slip/contact mechanisms.
The proposed mechanism attribution adds no discriminating observation beyond generic 'slip causes stiffness loss'.

candidates.contribution: Integrated vacuum-layer-jamming M->R->E scientific act: baseline continuum model M1 -> interface-resolved reference R -> independent experiment E, used to map where M1 is valid, where it breaks down, and why.

known_overlap.overlap: Strong M->R overlap and error-boundary mapping, but not vacuum layer jamming and lacks physical E.
Layer-jamming model + FEA + experiment, but not a systematic validity/breakdown map of Zhang-type M1.
Layer-jamming analytical model + experiment with slip mechanisms, but not the same M1 validity question.
Layer-jamming continuum model construction/verification at RVE level, not M->R->E breakdown mapping.

kill_conditions: A substantially equivalent prior study integrates M->R->E for vacuum layer-jamming beams and maps validity/breakdown of the same conceptual continuum model.
The integrated act decomposes into only routine known steps with no new discriminating scientific question or boundary.

explicit_non_candidates: Creating a new continuum layer-jamming model.
Using vacuum pressure to tune layer-jamming stiffness.
Observing interlayer slip, hysteresis, or stiffness change.
Using full-contact FE as a reference.
Comparing model predictions with experiments in a generic sense.
Using a 5% or other numerical error threshold by itself.
Claiming multi-layer partial interaction is absent from prior art.

high_threats_requiring_later_gate.reason: Closest same-act threat: M->R plus quantitative error boundary; must be explicitly attacked in K2/K3/K4/K7/K9.
Closest continuum layer-jamming homogenization prior art; must be used to prevent model-creation novelty migration.
